supporting_news.title: India benchmark bond posts worst day in six months on RBI measures
supporting_news.summary: Indian government bonds experienced a significant decline due to central bank measures aimed at draining liquidity. The benchmark 10-year bond yield rose to its highest level in three years, signaling potential rate hikes. Consumer inflation increased to 5.54%, exceeding forecasts and raising concerns over future monetary policy. The Reserve Bank of India announced bond sales and changes to cash reserve ratio maintenance.

supporting_news.title: India’s 10-year bond yield hits 3-year high as RBI’s liquidity measure weighs on demand
supporting_news.summary: Indian government bonds extended losses on Monday, pushing the benchmark 10-year yield to a three-year high as the RBI’s latest liquidity-tightening measures added to selling pressure. Tighter banking-system liquidity can curb banks’ capacity to invest in government securities, weakening bond demand and pushing prices lower and yields higher.

supporting_news.title: RBI measures, intervention spark rupee's sharpest rally in six months
supporting_news.summary: On Monday, the Indian rupee gained about 1% after the Reserve Bank of India announced measures to curb dollar demand. Oil companies' dollar purchases will now be directed away from the spot market, easing pressure on the rupee. This intervention aims to address the mounting balance of payments challenges due to high oil prices. However, analysts remain cautious about the sustainability of the rupee's recovery moving forward.

supporting_news.title: Rupee rebounds nearly 1% after RBI moves to curb speculative trades
supporting_news.summary: The rupee rebounded nearly 1% to 95.77 per dollar on Monday after the RBI announced measures to curb speculative currency trades. A special window for state-owned oil marketing companies eased spot-market pressure, though dollar buying by importers and corporates capped gains. Elevated crude prices and global uncertainties continue to weigh on the currency.

supporting_news.title: Will RBI’s CRR hike to 99% hit HDFC, SBI and other bank stocks? Here’s what Jefferies says
supporting_news.summary: The RBI has raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement to 99% from 90% from October 16 to curb banking system liquidity. Jefferies expects a limited impact on banks’ net interest margins, estimating a potential 1-2 basis point increase in funding costs. It prefers banks over NBFCs in a rising-rate environment and sees up to 47% upside in Bandhan Bank.
